chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Ja'far, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Musayyab, who said:
Al-Abd al-Salih (peace be upon him) said: 'Adhere to the Laft (turnip), so eat it, meaning the turnip, for there is no one except that he has a vein of leprosy, and the Laft dissolves it.'

key_terms.السَّلْجَم: As-Saljam, a specific type of turnip or radish
key_terms.اللِّفْت: Al-Laft, a term for turnip or a dish made from it
key_terms.الْعَبْدُ الصَّالِحُ: Al-Abd al-Salih (The Servant of God), a title for Musa ibn Ja'far (AS)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual and physical benefit of eating turnips according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam Musa al-Kazim (peace be upon him), titled Al-Abd al-Salih, prescribes turnips (*Al-Laft*) as a prophylactic against leprosy (*Al-Judham*), asserting that every human possesses a latent predisposition to the disease. This reflects the Shia tradition of integrating practical medicine with spiritual health, viewing dietary choices as a means to purify the body from inherent weaknesses. The emphasis on 'dissolving' the vein of leprosy underscores the concept of preventative care within the Imams' medical teachings.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Abdullah Bin Ja’far, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ali Bin Al Musayyab who said,

‘Al-Abd Al-Salihasws (7th Imamasws) said: ‘It is upon you with (eating) Al-Lafti (a turnip dish), so eat it, meaning the turnip, for there is no one except for him is a vein for the leprosy, and Al-Lafti removes it’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from ‘Abd Allah ibn Ja‘far from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Ali ibn Musayyib who has said the following:
“The virtuous servant (of Allah) has said, ‘You must eat al-Luft, that is, turnips; everyone has a vein of leprosy and al-Luft dissolves it.’”
